sources.content: Red blood cells, also called erythrocytes, carry oxygen from the lungs to the tissues of the body. They are packed with hemoglobin, an iron-containing protein that binds oxygen and gives blood its red colour. A mature human red blood cell has no nucleus, which leaves more room for hemoglobin. The cells have a flattened disc shape that is thinner in the middle than at the edge, and they measure about 7 to 8 micrometres across.

In adults, red blood cells are made in the bone marrow, a process called erythropoiesis. The kidneys control the rate by releasing a hormone called erythropoietin when oxygen levels in the blood fall. A red blood cell lasts about 120 days in circulation. Old cells are removed mainly by the spleen and the liver. A healthy adult has about 4 to 6 million red blood cells in each microlitre of blood.
